items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. holds average inventory worth €200,000. Annual holding costs (storage, insurance, waste and the cost of capital) are 25% of the value of inventory. Moving to just-in-time (JIT) would cut average inventory by 80% but add €14,400 a year in extra delivery costs. Calculate the net annual saving from JIT.
items.answer: New average inventory = €40,000; holding cost saving = (€200,000 − €40,000) × 25% = €40,000; net saving = €40,000 − €14,400 = €25,600.
items.markingKey: 200,000 × (1 − 80%) = 40,000; saving 40,000; net 25,600. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for net saving. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.answer: New average inventory = $100,000; holding cost saving = ($500,000 − $100,000) × 20% = $80,000; net saving = $80,000 − $9,600 = $70,400.
items.markingKey: 500,000 × (1 − 80%) = 100,000; saving 80,000; net 70,400. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for net saving. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.

items.stem: Define the term "just-in-time (JIT)".
items.answer: A stock control system in which materials arrive just when needed for production, so little stock is held
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a stock control system in which materials arrive just when needed for production, so little stock is held. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: A firm that produced 10,000 units with 250 defects has a defect rate of:
Which of the following best describes "supplier partnership"?
options: Increasing the pace or pressure of work, which can result from lean methods
A long-term, close relationship with suppliers based on trust, quality and reliable deliveries
An international standard certifying that a firm has an effective quality management system
Inspecting products, usually at the end of production, to find and remove defects
items.answer: A long-term, close relationship with suppliers based on trust, quality and reliable deliveries
items.markingKey: B. "supplier partnership" is a long-term, close relationship with suppliers based on trust, quality and reliable deliveries.

items.stem: Explain the difference between quality control and quality assurance.
items.answer: Quality control detects defects by inspecting finished products; quality assurance prevents defects by setting standards and checking them throughout production.
items.markingKey: Quality control detects defects by inspecting finished products; quality assurance prevents defects by setting standards and checking them throughout production. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Tasman Surf Co. produces 8,000 units a month with a defect rate of 3%. Each defective unit costs £12 to rework. A total quality management (TQM) programme costing £30,000 a year would cut the defect rate to 0.5%. Calculate the number of defective units each month before and after, the annual saving in rework costs, and whether the programme is financially worthwhile.
items.answer: Defects: 240 → 40 a month; annual saving = (240 − 40) × £12 × 12 = £28,800; net = −£1,200 a year, so the programme is not justified on rework savings alone. Non-financial benefits include fewer complaints and a better reputation.
items.markingKey: 8,000 × 3% and × 0.5%; difference × 12 × 12 = 28,800; compare with 30,000. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for saving and judgement. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts.
